Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Ankit Bisht, learned counsel holding 
brief of Mr. Vinay Kumar, learned counsel for 
the petitioner.
2. Mr. Harshit Bisht, learned counsel holding 
brief of Mr. Siddhartha Sah, learned counsel for 
the respondents-Bank. 
3. By means of the writ petition, petitioner 
has sought the indulgence of this Court for a 
direction to the respondent-Bank to sanction 
the pension to the petitioner as per the 
provisions contained in the circular dated 
21.05.2010 issued by the erstwhile Allahabad 
Bank (now Indian Bank). 
4. Learned counsel for the respondents 
prays for and is granted six weeks’ time to file 
counter affidavit.
5. Thereafter, two weeks’ time is granted to 
the petitioner to file rejoinder affidavit.
6. List on 30.08.2024.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
34 WPSS No. 821 of 2024
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Ms. Sudha Tamta, Advocate, holding 
brief of Mr. Vinay Kumar, Advocate for the 
petitioner.
Mr. Siddharth Sah, Advocate for the 
respondents.
The respondents has not filed counter 
affidavit despite multiple opportunities 
having been given.
On 02.06.2025, while granting 
opportunity to the respondents to file 
counter affidavit, this Court has noted then 
“No extension of time shall be granted to 
any of the parties for completing the 
pleadings”.
Today again on behalf of the 
respondents time is sought for filing 
counter affidavit.
List this matter for final hearing on 
28.07.2025 as a first case after fresh. 
Meanwhile, if the respondents still 
propose to file counter affidavit, it may be 
filed within a week. A week thereafter, 
rejoinder affidavit, if any, may be filed.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 08.07.2025
Jitendra
